subject: Deep tailback: Helion checkout SLA breach & exec sync
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@helioncommerce.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p99 spike on checkout - urgent

Monica / Ben —

We're seeing a massive p99 increase on checkout calls to the Redwood hosted endpoint starting ~08:50 PDT. Latency jumped from ~300ms to >6s and a spike in 500s (roughly 2.3% of traffic) coincided. This is impacting a subset of customers and our checkout abandonment metric is already up.

Attached is a short telemetry dump (helion-sla-telemetry.csv) showing token counts, route IDs and timestamps. We also captured a demo recording where the spinner never resolves (demo-recording.mp4).

Can you confirm whether this looks like a model-level performance regression or something in your serving infra (queueing/backpressure)? We have a mid-morning executive check and need a quick triage summary.

- Alex
Alex Torres
Head of Engineering, Helion Commerce
alex.torres@helioncommerce.com

Attachments: helion-sla-telemetry.csv (csv), demo-recording.mp4 (mp4)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 7 Jun 2028 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike on checkout - urgent

Thanks Alex — and Ben / Eng team FYI.

Quick summary from our side after a first pass:
- We've seen correlated queue depth growth on the public route serving Helion between 08:48–08:55 PDT.
- Concurrent connection counts jumped for that tenant's model variant; there's evidence of request queuing and fallback to a lower-capacity shard.
- No recent model pushes on our catalog for that family in the last 24h.

Immediate asks:
1) Ben — can you confirm contract / SLA expectations so we can call the right execs?
2) Evelyn / Karthik — please pull p95/p99 traces by route + shard, and check the concurrency caps and any recent autoscaler activity.
3) Alex — if you can share any client-side recent change (client SDK, request bundling) that would be helpful.

I'm setting up a 30-min bridge in 10 min and will include Rishi for an exec-level update. Attaching our short runbook (p99-runbook.pdf) with recommended mitigation steps: bump concurrency temporarily, enable prefix caching for the heaviest routes, and fallback routing to dedicated capacity if latencies do not recover.

Monica Patel
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

On Wed, Jun 7, 2028 at 9:32 AM Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'm setting up a 30-min bridge in 10 min and will include Rishi for an exec-level update.

Notes from initial triage (telco + quick logs):
- Root symptom: sustained request queuing on route /v1/helion/checkout at the router layer — queue depth rose ~x6 over baseline.
- Probable proximate cause: aggressive concurrency cap hit on a hot shard combined with a transient burst of high-token requests from Helion (client-side change?). When shards hit cap, we queue requests; when queue exceeds our internal cutoff we batch-evict which increases p99 quickly and leads to downstream 5xx as KV cache misses increase.
- Autoscaler behavior: we saw delayed scale-up for that sharded group due to recent conservative thresholds (tuned to avoid overscaling).

Immediate mitigations applied (10:00–10:10 PDT):
1) Temporarily increased concurrency cap for the affected shard -> visible p95 improvement.
2) Enabled prefix/KV cache warming on the most common prefixes for Helion routes.
3) Opened a controlled fallback path to a dedicated low-latency pool for critical checkout routes in case recovery stalls.

Next actions (owner):
- Karthik: follow up with infra team to adjust autoscaler thresholds and add a short-term policy to allow rapid scale for tenant-score > 0.8.
- Monica / Ben: update Helion execs that mitigation is in flight and we expect measurable p99 recovery in 15–30 minutes.
- Rishi: please confirm if we want a temporary credit offer and exec-level note templates.

Attaching a short diagnostic snippet and the runbook steps used. Will follow up with a forensic log dump.

Evelyn Hart
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: diagnostic-snippet.txt (text), p99-runbook.pdf (pdf)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@helioncommerce.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@helioncommerce.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Jun 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-mortem note & exec sync (Helion checkout)

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for your patience. Quick post-mortem summary and next steps after the bridge and forensic analysis:

What happened
- A client-side traffic pattern change (larger tokenized payloads from a new A/B check) caused a burst of high-cost requests. One hot shard hit its configured concurrency cap; conservative autoscaler thresholds delayed scale-up and caused requests to queue. Queue exhaustion and KV cache churn triggered downstream 5xxs and the observed p99 surge.

What we did in 60 minutes
- Bumped concurrency cap on the affected shard and adjusted autoscaler run thresholds (temporary TTL = 4 hours).
- Enabled prefix/KV caching and started a cache-warm routine for top prefixes.
- Opened a controlled fallback to dedicated capacity for checkout route.
- Eng team ran a targeted log export and we validated p99 returned to ~800ms within 25 minutes after mitigations.

Customer impact and remediation
- Impact window: ~08:48–10:12 PDT on Jun 7, 2028. Approx affected traffic: 3.2% of requests for Helion checkout routes showed >2s latency; 2.3% observed 5xx.
- Ben will handle SLA credit discussions. Recommended first offer: service credit covering 50% of affected-minute cost for the impacted window, pending final exec sign-off.

Follow-ups (owners & ETA)
- Permanent autoscaler tuning: Karthik / Infra -> proposal in 48h.
- Improve tenant burst detection & automatic emergency scale path: Evelyn -> draft by EOD + test plan.
- Customer-facing summary & credit confirmation: Ben -> 24h.
- Engineering forensic log export shared in Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/helion-sla-telemetry

We will schedule a 30-minute exec sync tomorrow to walk through the root cause and long-term mitigations. Alex, please let us know if you want a conference for the exec sync or prefer a summary doc.

Apologies for the disruption — we take this seriously and will adjust our emergency scaling playbook to reduce time-to-recovery.

Best,

Monica Patel
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
